route: Courmayeur → Mont Blanc Tunnel → Chamonix → Switzerland → Strasbourg
intro:
Leaving Courmayeur this morning, the clouds were hanging low over the mountains. Everything was gray and overcast as I said goodbye to Italy and headed toward the Mont Blanc Tunnel.

The tunnel seemed to go on forever. Blue lights marked the following distance, and as I drove, I kept thinking about where I actually was - underneath that enormous mountain. After seeing Mont Blanc from above yesterday, traveling beneath it today was amazing in a completely different way.

Coming out on the French side near Chamonix felt like entering another day. There was blue sky overhead, wisps of cloud down in the valley, and sunlight peeking over the mountains and lighting up their tips. From dark and gray to bright mountain sunshine, all through one tunnel.

The descent had beautiful views, but some stretches were harrowing. There were exposed edges where I couldn’t see a guardrail, cars behind me, and turns that had me braking harder than I wanted. It was difficult to enjoy the scenery while concentrating so much on the road.

Later, traveling through Switzerland, the landscape changed again. Vineyards, rolling hills, and Lake Geneva off to my left replaced the dramatic mountain scenery. At times, I found myself wondering whether I was in Switzerland or France - the countryside seemed to blend together. About halfway through Switzerland, the sky became overcast and stayed that way for the rest of the day.

Before crossing back into France, I drove through a town where school seemed to have just let out. Maybe it was a half day. There were so many little children walking around - some looked younger than five - while cars drove quickly through town. It was amazing to see children that small making their way around with all that traffic passing by.

Entering France, the land opened up. Flat stretches of farmland spread out across the landscape, another change from the mountains I had left that morning.

One of the harder parts of today’s drive was feeling that the mountain-and-country portion of the trip was slipping behind me. Even with those stretches of farmland, the driving felt increasingly packed with cities and traffic. I missed being surrounded by the mountains.
